A popular choice for ski families who want more than a basic room without paying mountain resort prices.
name: Kinross Inn
short_description: Well-appointed motel with indoor heated pool; short walk from CBD restaurants.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | smart_tv_netflix | air_conditioning | heating | electric_blankets | microwave | toaster | fridge | kettle | daily_housekeeping | garden
long_description: White Manor Motel consistently earns top TripAdvisor scores for cleanliness and is one of the best mid-range options in Cooma. The 12 air-conditioned rooms (queen, twin, family) feature smart TVs with Netflix, microwave, toaster, and fridge. The property sits on Sharp Street with mountain backdrop views. Small and personal — the antithesis of the highway chain motel.
name: White Manor Motel
short_description: Highly-rated family-run motel 1.1 km from CBD; 12 immaculate rooms with mountain views.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | air_conditioning | heating | fridge | tea_coffee | daily_housekeeping
long_description: Nestled in central Cooma, the Nebula Motel pitches itself as a boutique stay within walking distance of all town amenities — shops, restaurants, pubs, and the Visitors Centre. Popular with skiers who want to be on foot for the evening without needing a car. The motel has a solid review base (249 TripAdvisor reviews) and consistent scores for location and value.
name: Nebula Motel
short_description: Central boutique motel on Bombala Street; walking distance to shops and restaurants.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | air_conditioning | heating | fridge | tea_coffee
long_description: The Altair Motel is a purpose-designed boutique motel on Sharp Street aiming for a homely atmosphere — a notch above the standard highway motel. Positive TripAdvisor scores (3.8 from 75 reviews) reflect comfortable rooms and friendly service. Centrally located near cafes and snowsports hire shops. Contact is primarily mobile-first.
name: Altair Motel
short_description: Boutique-style motel on Sharp Street designed as a home-away-from-home.

amenities: free_parking | air_conditioning | heating | electric_blankets | bar | open_fire | restaurant | bbq | pool_outdoor_summer | recreation_room | karaoke | cots
long_description: The High Country Motel on Chapman Street offers 40 rooms set in a quiet bush-adjacent location, away from highway noise. Amenities include an outdoor pool (summer only), bar with open fire, licensed restaurant, karaoke, and BBQ area. Well-suited to larger groups and coach tours. Renovated rooms include microwaves and bar fridges. Accepts credit cards.
name: High Country Motel
short_description: Quiet 40-unit motel with outdoor pool, bar, and restaurant; great for groups and coach tours.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | ev_chargers | air_conditioning | heating | fridge | kettle | bar | open_fire | restaurant | ski_hire_adjacent | laundry | soundproof_rooms
long_description: The Cooma Motor Lodge (6 Sharp Street, Golden Chain member) has been a Cooma institution since 1965 and was renovated in 2007. With 44 rooms on two floors and EV chargers recently installed, it suits road-trippers and snowfield-bound drivers alike. It sits directly next to Rhythm Snowsports ski hire, making it exceptionally practical for ski season. The in-house bistro and log fire bar create an après-ski atmosphere.
name: Cooma Motor Lodge
short_description: 44-room Golden Chain motel next to Rhythm Snowsports hire; EV chargers on-site.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | air_conditioning | bar | bistro | open_fire | secure_parking_motorcycles | atm | conference_space | wheelchair_accessible_parking
long_description: The Alpine Hotel on Sharp Street is a renovated two-storey pub hotel with 27 guestrooms, an open fire lounge, and a bistro serving lunch and dinner 7 days. With 10 beers on tap and secure garage parking for motorcycles, it caters to a wide mix of travellers. Ranked #1 Best Value in Cooma on TripAdvisor. Pet policy: no pets. Airport shuttle: not available.
name: Alpine Hotel
short_description: Central pub hotel with 27 rooms, bistro, and 10 beers on tap; TripAdvisor #1 best-value.

address: 59-61 Lambie Street (cnr Sharp & Lambie), Cooma NSW 2630
amenities: bar | bistro | games_room | shared_bathrooms | heater | towels_linen | front_verandah_dining
long_description: The Royal Hotel is a heritage-listed two-storey dressed-freestone pub on the corner of Sharp and Lambie Streets, built in 1858 and listed on the NSW State Heritage Register in 1999. Pub-style rooms (shared bathrooms) are budget-priced — great for skiers on a tight budget. The Royal Bistro serves traditional Australian pub meals Tuesday–Sunday. The building's Georgian/Victorian character makes it one of Cooma's most photographed landmarks.
name: Royal Hotel Cooma
short_description: NSW State Heritage-listed sandstone pub (1858) with budget pub rooms and a popular bistro.

amenities: bar | bistro | drive_through_bottle_shop | cinema | function_rooms
long_description: Built in 1862, the Cooma Hotel on the corner of Massie and Vale Streets claims the title of Cooma's oldest continually operating hotel. Beyond accommodation, it functions as a community hub with bar, bistro serving lunch and dinner, drive-through bottle shop, cinema, and function facilities. Budget pub-style rooms are available. Phone updated to +61 2 6404 7530 under new management.
name: Cooma Hotel
short_description: Oldest continuously operating hotel in Cooma (1862); bar, bistro, drive-through bottle shop.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | breakfast_included | central_heating | en_suite | garden | library | parlour | off_street_parking
long_description: Ellstanmor Country Guesthouse occupies an 1875 Victorian home on Massie Street in the heart of Cooma's CBD. The property features ornate staircases, French doors, a library, parlour, and 4 queen rooms each with en-suite. Guests are served self-service continental or cooked-to-order country breakfasts. A treadmill, astronomical telescope, and genuine character distinguish this B&B from any motel. Rated #1 B&B in Cooma and in the top 10% of TripAdvisor properties globally.
name: Ellstanmor Country Guesthouse
short_description: Victorian-era B&B (1875) in Cooma CBD with 4 en-suite rooms; TripAdvisor #1 B&B.

amenities: fully_equipped_kitchen | outdoor_kitchen_bbq | underfloor_hydronic_heating | luxury_bathrooms | linen_bedding | smart_appliances | private_backyard | self_contained | no_wifi_noted
long_description: Nest Stays comprises two lovingly restored 1860s heritage terrace homes on picturesque Lambie Street, curated by Australian fashion retailer birdsnest. Terrace 1 sleeps 6 adults across 3 bedrooms; Terrace 2 sleeps 6 across 4 bedrooms with an oversized stone bath. Both feature fully equipped kitchens, cosy lounges, underfloor hydronic heating, 100% linen bedding, iKou organic bath products, and private backyard patios with outdoor kitchens. TripAdvisor's top-rated property in Cooma (5.0/5, 24 reviews). Perfect for girlfriend groups or ski families wanting a premium basecamp.
name: Nest Stays by Birdsnest
short_description: Two boutique heritage terraces on Lambie Street by fashion brand birdsnest; luxury self-contained.

address: 286 Sharp Street (Snowy Mountains Hwy), Cooma NSW 2630
amenities: cabins_self_contained | powered_sites | unpowered_sites | bbq_area | camp_kitchen | mini_golf | playground | activity_room | modern_amenities | drive_through_sites
long_description: Formerly the Cooma Snowy Mountains Tourist Park and now operating as Cooma Holiday Park, this central park at 286 Sharp Street sits on the Snowy Mountains Highway. Options range from self-contained Banksia Cabins (2 bedrooms, full kitchen, sleeps 4) to budget Snowgum Cabins and powered/unpowered caravan sites from $35/night. Facilities include mini golf, playground, activity room, and BBQ areas. Walking distance to town centre shops and cafes. The budget option for families and van travellers.
name: Cooma Holiday Park
short_description: Family-friendly caravan park in central Cooma with cabins, powered and unpowered sites.

address: 651 Snowy Mountains Highway, Pine Valley, Cooma NSW 2630
amenities: free_parking | air_conditioning | heating | fridge | tea_coffee | bbq | complimentary_coffee | roadhouse_cafe_adjacent
long_description: The Alpine Country Motel (formerly Alpine Country Motor Inn) sits at 651 Snowy Mountains Highway on the approach from Jindabyne, 4–5 minutes south of central Cooma. On 4 acres of land with a Metro Roadhouse café attached, it's the first stop heading toward the ski fields from Cooma. Complimentary coffee for guests. The cheapest bookable rates in the Cooma area, often from $117/night.
name: Alpine Country Motel
short_description: Roadside motel on Snowy Mountains Hwy 5 km south of Cooma CBD; adjacent Metro Roadhouse café.

amenities: breakfast_included | free_wifi | free_parking
long_description: Cromwell House is a boutique guesthouse property in central Cooma with exceptional TripAdvisor scores (4.9/5 from 49 reviews), indicating a genuinely outstanding guest experience. The property includes breakfast and is listed in the TripAdvisor B&B/inn category. It represents Cooma's premium heritage accommodation tier alongside Ellstanmor and Nest Stays.
name: Cromwell House
short_description: Boutique B&B; highly-rated heritage-style guesthouse near Cooma CBD (TripAdvisor 4.9/5).

amenities: central_heating | tv | fridge | tea_coffee | toaster | cots | babysitting | parking | self_contained_units
long_description: The Bunkhouse Motel on Soho Street is a budget-friendly option with 29 units — 18 standard rooms and 11 self-contained units with cooking facilities. Ground-floor access, central heating, TV, and babysitting availability make it popular with budget ski families. One block from the Cooma Ex-Services Club (RSL) and central to the main street strip.
name: Bunkhouse Motel
short_description: Budget 29-unit motel centrally located 1 block from the RSL club; some self-contained units.

amenities: free_wifi | free_parking | air_conditioning | heating | fridge | tea_coffee
long_description: The Alkira Motel earns strong TripAdvisor marks (4.1/5, 71 reviews) and appears repeatedly in best-value and family-friendly shortlists for Cooma. Located close to the Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre and within reach of the town's cafes and snowsports hire shops. A solid mid-tier option for those prioritising cleanliness and value.
name: Alkira Motel
short_description: Well-reviewed motel near the Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre; family-friendly, TripAdvisor 4.1.

amenities: onsen | rotenburo | private_spa | sauna | restaurant | bar | parking | wifi | shuttle_to_station | shuttle_to_snow_monkey_park
long_description: Yorozuya is one of Yudanaka's most storied inns, blending Meiji-era elegance with modern comforts. Its showpiece is the Momoyama-buro (桃山風呂), a stunning wooden bathhouse registered as a Tangible Cultural Property of Japan, featuring soaring ceilings and ornate joinery. The property offers both indoor and outdoor rotenburo, kaiseki cuisine using north-Nagano mountain and river produce, and — since 2023 — a private spa suite called 'Bon'. Shuttle service available to Yudanaka Station and Snow Monkey Park.
name: Yorozuya
notes: Momoyama-buro is a registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan. Private SPA 'Bon' opened Feb 2023 — 2 sauna types + private bath. Highly recommended for special occasions.
short_description: Historic prestige ryokan with a nationally registered cultural property bathhouse (Momoyama-buro) and abundant natural hot spring flow.

amenities: onsen | rotenburo | private_bath_reservable | jacuzzi | restaurant | bar | lounge | massage | karaoke | wifi | shuttle_to_station | shuttle_to_snow_monkey_park | shuttle_to_ski_area | day_trip_bathing_available
long_description: Named after the famous haiku poet Kobayashi Issa who was born in nearby Kashiwabara, this ryokan sits in central Yudanaka and manages three hot spring sources producing soft alkaline water (弱アルカリ性単純泉) prized for skin-beautifying properties. All baths are 100% kakenagashi (continuously flowing, never recycled). Rooms range from classic Japanese tatami to Japanese-Western hybrid and premium suites with private outdoor baths. The property offers a free shuttle to Yudanaka Station, Snow Monkey Park, and Shiga Kogen ski areas, with an English hotline operated by an English-speaking coordinator.
name: Hotel Issa-tei / Issa no Komichi Biyu no Yado
name_local: 一茶のこみち 美湯の宿
notes: English hotline: 080-6938-3361 (Craig Shaw). Day-trip bathing available ¥800. Private reserved bath ¥3,000 for 2 places. Free shuttle to Shiga Kogen ski areas is a major benefit for skiers. Tattoo policy: private baths available — public bath policy not explicitly confirmed as tattoo-friendly.
short_description: Mid-sized onsen ryokan with 100% natural flowing hot springs including a rooftop outdoor bath and renowned hot spring management by an in-house 'onsen meister'.

address: 1410 Hirao, Kambayashi Onsen, Yamanouchi, Shimotakai-gun, Nagano 381-0401
amenities: onsen | rotenburo | private_bath_reservable | indoor_heated_pool | restaurant | lounge | garden | wifi | free_parking | shuttle_from_yudanaka_station
long_description: Senjukaku sits at the end of the road near the Snow Monkey Park trailhead in Kambayashi Onsen, a quieter sister village to Yudanaka. The hotel boasts the largest natural hot spring source in Nagano Prefecture — 720 litres per minute, constantly drained for freshness — with communal indoor and outdoor baths, and private hinoki cypress or granite kashikiri baths (¥1,500/45 min). The traditional Japanese garden with 100-year-old sakura trees, koi stream, and lobby art exhibitions lend an atmosphere of cultivated elegance. Kaiseki meals use Shinshu beef, golden gamefowl, and seasonal local vegetables. Catering to international guests including for vegetarian and gluten-free dietary needs.
name: Kambayashi Hotel Senjukaku
notes: Note from Expedia: 'some properties do not permit guests with tattoos to use the onsite public bathing facilities' — public baths likely not_allowed for tattooed guests; private baths available. Can cater to vegetarian, gluten-free, dietary restrictions if requested at reservation. Indoor heated pool free (bring swimsuit). The largest natural hot spring source in Nagano Prefecture.
short_description: Closest ryokan to Snow Monkey Park, with Nagano Prefecture's largest hot spring source and luxurious kaiseki dining.

amenities: onsen | private_bath_reservable | restaurant | wifi | parking
long_description: Shimaya (島屋) is a quietly elegant, old-style ryokan that has maintained traditional hospitality for generations in the heart of Yudanaka. The property features three bathing options: the hinoki (Japanese cypress) bath called 'Hagi no Yu' (萩の湯), the communal large bath 'Shiga no Yu' (志賀の湯), and a private rental bath. All hot springs are 100% natural source water. The proprietor Mr. Yumoto is known for fast communication in English by email. Unlike most ryokan, food is offered as an add-on (not automatically included), making it a more flexible and affordable option. Meals are Japanese home-style cooking using seasonal local ingredients.
name: Shimaya Ryokan
notes: Meal plan is flexible — breakfast ¥800-1,300, dinner ¥2,500-4,500 as add-ons. Good-value choice. Shimaya Soba restaurant is a separate establishment (see eats). Owner responds to English emails. Price range may vary — ¥24,000-29,000/room based on TripAdvisor data.
short_description: Traditional family-run ryokan with flowing hinoki cypress hot spring bath, communal bath, and private rental bath.

amenities: onsen | rotenburo | private_bath_reservable | restaurant | souvenir_shop | wifi | parking | massage
long_description: Tawaraya Ryokan is a 10-room traditional inn set around a tranquil garden in central Yudanaka, a 5-minute walk from the station. The outdoor garden rotenburo can be reserved privately (30-minute slots) and has drawn consistent praise from international guests as one of the most atmospheric baths in the area. Staff are well-regarded for their English ability and warm service. Rooms feature tatami mats, futon bedding, and shoji screens. Kaiseki multi-course dinners featuring seasonal local produce and Shinshu beef, with a Japanese set breakfast. Souvenir shop on site.
name: Tawaraya Ryokan
notes: Highly rated for English service and private garden onsen. 'Amazing kaiseki meals worth ordering in advance.' — Guest review. Rooms have private toilet but shared bathrooms (shared with Japanese facilities).
short_description: Charming small ryokan with reservable private outdoor onsen garden bath, English-speaking staff, and excellent kaiseki meals.

amenities: onsen | rotenburo | jacuzzi | private_bath_some_rooms | restaurant | terrace | boutique_shop | wifi | parking
long_description: Aburaya Tousen is a stylish mid-luxury ryokan blending traditional aesthetics with contemporary design touches. Located about an 8-minute walk from Yudanaka Station, it is particularly popular with couples and international guests. Rooms include suites with private open-air onsen baths on balconies, and the communal baths include an outdoor rooftop rotenburo with panoramic views and a jacuzzi. The on-site restaurant serves kaiseki cuisine for dinner in private dining rooms. An on-site boutique carries premium regional crafts and chopsticks. Staff are noted for being thoughtful and welcoming to international guests.
name: Aburaya Tousen
notes: #8 of 81 onsen ryokan in Yamanouchi on TripAdvisor. Owner greeted guests personally. Known for excellent chopsticks in gift shop. Some staff speak English. Rooftop rotenburo particularly praised.
short_description: Upscale modern ryokan with private room onsen, rooftop rotenburo, and in-house boutique and gift shop.

amenities: onsen | restaurant | wifi | parking
long_description: Uotoshi Ryokan (魚敏) is a compact 8-room inn offering an authentic low-key ryokan experience in Yudanaka. The communal onsen is separated by gender and is open 24 hours, with the traditional mineral water providing a pleasantly aromatic and perfectly tempered soak. Rooms are spacious Japanese-style with excellent mountain and valley views; balcony rooms facing the fountain are particularly recommended by guests. The half-board rate is standard and meals must be confirmed before check-in. Located just 500 metres from Yudanaka Station.
name: Uotoshi Ryokan
notes: Rated $71-99 USD per room (TripAdvisor). Half-board guests must check in by 6pm for dinner. 24-hour public bath. Highly affordable by Yudanaka standards. TripAdvisor rating 4.3/5 from 36 reviews.
short_description: Small traditional ryokan with gender-separated communal onsen and rooms overlooking the valley, 500m from Yudanaka Station.

amenities: onsen | restaurant | parking
long_description: Honke Bansho (本家伴勝) is a long-standing traditional ryokan in the Yudanaka Onsen district. As a 'honke' (main house) property, it emphasises traditional hospitality rooted in Nagano inn-keeping heritage. The property offers communal hot spring bathing and seasonal kaiseki-style meals featuring Shinshu regional specialities including river fish from the Chikuma River, wild mountain vegetables (sansai), and local mushrooms. The intimate atmosphere suits travellers seeking an authentic Japanese inn experience away from larger hotel crowds.
name: Honke Bansho
notes: Note: Do not confuse with 'Honke Bankyu' (本家伴久) which is a separate, unrelated luxury ryokan in Yunishigawa Onsen, Nikko (Tochigi Prefecture). Honke Bansho is specific to Yudanaka. Limited online booking availability — best booked via Jalan or Rakuten Travel. English spoken is limited to no.
short_description: Traditional Yudanaka ryokan with onsen and local Shinshu cuisine in central hot spring town.

amenities: onsen | sauna | steam_room | tea_bath | restaurant | lounge | wifi
long_description: Hotel Sanyokan (山陽館) is a large-format traditional hotel in Yudanaka Onsen with one of the most extensive onsen bath complexes in the town, featuring multiple pools including a tea bath, waterfall massage pool, sauna, and steam room. The sprawling layout and multiple bath types attract both ryokan guests and day-trippers. Rooms range from spacious tatami-style (some with mini-kitchenettes) to private Western rooms. The hotel has a communal lounge area with TV and tatami seating. A casual in-house kitchen/diner operates during meal hours. Located close to Yudanaka Station.
name: Hotel Sanyokan
notes: Note: 'Hotel Yudanaka' as listed on some OTA sites may refer to this property or an adjacent hotel — both are similar large-format budget onsen hotels near the station. The property has also served as a community bathhouse for locals. Free shuttle to Snow Monkey Park. Rated as one of the largest onsen complexes in Yudanaka town.
short_description: Mid-range hotel with large communal onsen complex — one of the biggest in Yudanaka — near the station.

amenities: private_onsen | restaurant | complimentary_transport | wifi
long_description: Yamazakiya is a small family-operated ryokan run by Akira and his family (mother Kiyoko is a beloved local figure) on the charming main street of Yudanaka. Unlike most ryokan in the area, all onsen baths are private-use only, meaning guests need never share the bath — a significant advantage for tattooed travellers or those seeking complete privacy. Akira also holds keys to two public onsen nearby for guests who want that option. Traditional kaiseki breakfast and dinner are exceptional, featuring ultra-fresh local produce. Complimentary car service to the station and Snow Monkey Park trailhead. Rooms are tatami with kotatsu (heated table), futon, and river view options.
name: Yudanaka Onsen Yamazakiya
name_local: 湯田中温泉 山崎屋
notes: Tattoo policy: ALLOWED in private baths — all baths are private-use only so tattoos are not an issue. Host Akira also has access to public onsen for guests who wish. Rated 9.x on Booking.com. Exceptional guest-host warmth. Yukata worn correctly taught by staff. Complimentary Shinshu apple given to guests. Highly recommended for first-time ryokan visitors.
short_description: Intimate family-run ryokan with private onsen access, genuine hospitality from host Akira and family, and complimentary transport to Snow Monkey Park.

amenities: onsen | private_bath_reservable | restaurant | wifi | free_parking
long_description: Ryokan Hakura is a 5-minute walk from Yudanaka Station and offers both Japanese tatami rooms and Western-style rooms. The house onsen (100% kakenagashi natural hot spring) can be booked privately by room in 50-minute slots, ensuring guests never have to share. Staff are multilingual (English and Japanese). Unusually for a rural Nagano ryokan, the kitchen caters to various dietary needs including vegetarian, Muslim, and allergy-specific requirements with advance notice. Seasonal kaiseki meals feature Shinshu beef and locally foraged ingredients. Breakfast included; dinner add-on recommended.
name: Yudanaka Ryokan Hakura
notes: Onsen available: 15:00-19:00 (shared access), 19:00-next day 9:00 (private booking by room, 50-min slots). Accommodates vegetarian, Muslim, allergy diets — request 24 hours in advance. Host owner is very helpful with transport arrangements. Also listed on Expedia under 'Ryokan near Shiga Kogen Ski Area'.
short_description: Well-regarded mid-range ryokan with private-use onsen booking system, multilingual staff, and dietary-accommodating kaiseki meals.

amenities: onsen | rotenburo | private_bath_some_rooms | wine_bar | restaurant | wifi | free_parking | shuttle_to_snow_monkey_park
long_description: Hotel Tsubakino is a relaxed and comfortable onsen hotel set in the hills above Yudanaka, offering both Japanese-style tatami rooms and Western rooms. The signature feature is the 5th-floor open-air rotenburo with panoramic mountain views — especially spectacular in winter snow. Private outdoor baths are available in select premium rooms. The hotel also features a charming nightly wine bar (an unexpected find in rural Nagano) and serves highly regarded Japanese breakfasts. Staff are described as attentive and helpful. A 'monkey bus' for day trips to Snow Monkey Park departs from the property.
name: Hotel Tsubakino
notes: Private outdoor rooftop onsen (5F) for couples available at additional cost. Nightly wine bar is a popular après-onsen hangout. Monkey bus departs daily. The private outdoor bath for a parent/child duo is highly reviewed.
short_description: Mid-range hotel with rooftop outdoor onsen on the 5th floor, nightly wine bar, and excellent Japanese breakfasts, about 10 minutes walk from the station.

amenities: private_onsen | kitchenette | restaurant | lounge | complimentary_fridge | balcony | free_parking
long_description: Hotarutei Villas are a pair of high-end self-contained villas built in 2017 adjacent to the historic Hotarutei restaurant (est. 1987) in Kanbayashi, an 8-minute walk from the Snow Monkey Park trail entrance. Each villa sleeps 2-4 and features a private natural hot spring bath (half indoor, half outdoor), two bedrooms, spacious living room, kitchenette, and balcony. Fridge comes stocked with complimentary water, Shinshu apple juice, fresh milk, gelato, and Yebisu beer. Seasonal course dining available at the attached restaurant. The villas are constructed from a historic farmhouse relocated from Niigata. The 7-Eleven on Route 292 is a 5-minute drive.
name: Hotarutei Villas
notes: Only 2 villas — books out fast in ski season and Snow Monkey peak season (Jan-Mar). Tattoo policy: ALLOWED — private baths only, no public bath on site. Price range: ¥22,000-74,000 per night (Snow Monkey Resorts listing). Nearest convenience store: 7-Eleven on R292 (5 min drive) or Lawson at Yudanaka Station (7 min drive / 50 min walk).
short_description: Exclusive 2-villa property next to Snow Monkey Park with private indoor-outdoor natural hot spring baths, full seasonal dining, and luxury self-contained villas.

amenities: breakfast | common_area | wifi | complimentary_tea_coffee
long_description: Aibiya is the primary budget accommodation option in Yudanaka, combining hostel practicality with ryokan-style warmth. The hosts are a Japanese-Korean couple who speak English fluently and provide personalised recommendations for the area. Accommodation ranges from 4-bed dormitories to private rooms in both tatami and Western styles. A daily breakfast combining Japanese and Western dishes is served. While Aibiya does not have its own onsen, the hosts can direct guests to nearby public hot spring baths. The guesthouse attracts a largely international crowd and is the social hub of the Yudanaka backpacker scene.
name: Aibiya
notes: Check-in cut-off 20:00 — contact property if arriving late. No onsen on-site; hosts direct guests to nearby public baths (access to public onsen in Yudanaka area is easy). Tattoo: ALLOWED — no public onsen on-site so no restrictions. Excellent English spoken. Rated 10/10 on Expedia for service.
short_description: International-friendly upscale hostel in central Yudanaka, run by a welcoming Japanese-Korean couple, with dorm beds and private rooms.

amenities: day_trip_onsen | restaurant | craft_brewery | parking
long_description: The Yudanaka Brewery Complex U is a contemporary multi-purpose tourist complex opened in 2022 that combines a craft brewery, restaurant, and day-trip onsen baths under one roof. While primarily a day-trip destination (see also in the Eats section for the restaurant), the complex also offers accommodation in modern rooms. The 2nd-floor day-trip onsen is open 10:00-18:00. On-site craft beers are brewed using water from Yudanaka Onsen spring water. The complex is a 5-minute drive from Yudanaka Station in the Sano area, with 30 parking spaces.
name: Yudanaka Brewery Complex U (Inn)
name_local: ゆダナカ ブルワリーコンプレックスU (宿泊)
notes: Primarily a day-trip complex. Day-trip onsen and restaurant open 10:00-18:00. Food LO: 17:00. Parking: 30 spaces free. QR-code ordering in English available. Accommodation confirmation needs direct contact with property. Also listed in eats as 'yudanaka-brewery-complex-u'.
short_description: Modern craft-brewery-anchored complex with accommodation, day-trip onsen on the 2nd floor, and on-site Shinshu food and beer.

address: Yamanouchi, Shimotakai-gun, Nagano (booking service — various properties)
amenities: english_support | ski_pass_booking | transfers | local_activities
long_description: Snow Monkey Resorts is an English-language booking and concierge service specialising in the Yamanouchi region — Yudanaka, Snow Monkey Park, and Shiga Kogen. Rather than a single property, they represent multiple partner hotels and ryokan in the area, providing full English support for international travellers. Properties include Hotel Grand Phenix (Shiga Kogen), Hotel Sunny Shiga, T Hotel Ryuoo, and others. They also provide ski passes, transfers, and local activity booking. For travellers uncomfortable with Japanese-only booking systems, Snow Monkey Resorts provides a critical bridge.
name: Snow Monkey Resorts (Yamanouchi Area Booking Hub)
name_local: スノーモンキーリゾーツ
notes: This entry represents the Snow Monkey Resorts booking hub. Individual properties include Hotel Grand Phenix Okushiga, Hotel Sunny Shiga, T Hotel Ryuoo (Ryuoo Ski Park area). All properties booked via SMR include English concierge. Highly recommended for first-time visitors to the area. Partner property Kambayashi Hotel Senjukaku is also listed as a separate entry.
short_description: English-language concierge and booking service for Yamanouchi-area accommodation, including exclusive properties with full English support.

amenities: onsen | restaurant | wifi | cashless_payments
long_description: Masuya is a traditional ryokan in the Yudanaka Onsen area offering classic Japanese hospitality with a communal hot spring bath. The property is notable for explicitly accepting credit cards (unlike many rural Nagano establishments) and for its cashless payment capability — a practical advantage for international travellers. Guests must contact the property in advance to reserve public bathing access, and the property is transparent that some guests with tattoos may not be permitted to use the public bath — pointing tattooed travellers to contact in advance.
name: Wafu no Yado Masuya
notes: Tattoo policy: NOT ALLOWED in public bath (explicitly stated in Expedia notes). Accepts credit cards and cashless payments — unusual for Yudanaka. Reserve public bath access in advance (contact property). Guests with tattoos should inquire about alternative bathing options.
short_description: Traditional Japanese-style inn with communal hot spring bathing, accepting cards (no cash required), near Yudanaka Station.

amenities: self_contained | kitchen
long_description: Airbnb options in the Yamanouchi area are limited but include traditional kominka (古民家 — old Japanese farmhouse) rentals, private apartments in Nakano City (20 min drive), and occasional village houses in Yudanaka proper. These are ideal for groups or families wanting self-catering flexibility. Most Airbnb properties in this rural area do not include onsen; guests use public bathhouses (there are several in Yudanaka and Shibu Onsen villages). Tattoo policy is irrelevant for private rentals. English communication is available through the Airbnb platform with hosts.
name: Airbnb Listings — Yudanaka / Yamanouchi Area
name_local: エアビーアンドビー 湯田中・山ノ内エリア
notes: Airbnb supply in this area is thin. Check listings carefully for actual Yudanaka / Yamanouchi town location vs. Nakano City. Traditional kominka properties offer authentic Japanese rural atmosphere. No onsen on-site for most — use Yudanaka public baths or day-trip onsen at Brewery Complex U.
short_description: Private homes, kominka (old farmhouses), and apartments available via Airbnb in the broader Yudanaka / Yamanouchi area.

amenities: onsen | restaurant | wifi | parking
long_description: Yumotoya (湯元屋 — literally 'hot spring source house') is a traditional ryokan in central Yudanaka that emphasises family hospitality. The property offers communal gender-separated onsen and a kaiseki-style dinner featuring seasonal Shinshu specialties including river fish, wild mountain herbs, and local mushrooms, along with a Japanese breakfast. The name suggests the property draws directly from a natural hot spring source (yumoto). Suitable for both solo travellers and families. The property is within walking distance of Yudanaka Station.
name: Yumotoya
notes: Note: 'Yumotoya' (湯元屋) in Yudanaka should not be confused with 'Yumotoya' (ゆもとや) in Niigata/Iwamuro Onsen — they are completely different properties. Booking primarily via Jalan or Rakuten. Tattoo policy unconfirmed — contact property directly.
short_description: Family-oriented mid-sized ryokan with natural hot spring baths and traditional Shinshu cuisine in central Yudanaka.

amenities: ski_in_ski_out | onsen | restaurant
long_description: For skiers wanting ski-in/ski-out convenience, there are dozens of lodges, pensions (minshuku), and hotels directly on the Shiga Kogen plateau (1,500-2,000m elevation). These include the Hotel Grand Phenix Okushiga (luxury), Hotel Sunny Shiga (budget-friendly), and the Shiga Kogen Prince Hotel. Most are booked via Jalan or Rakuten in Japanese. The tradeoff: Shiga Kogen lodges have limited restaurant variety outside their own dining rooms, and the village atmosphere is less interesting than Yudanaka. For ski-school families or those who want to maximise slope time, on-mountain accommodation makes sense; for après-ski culture and onsen town experience, Yudanaka wins.
name: Shiga Kogen Ski Area Accommodation (via Yudanaka as base)
name_local: 志賀高原スキー場エリア宿泊
notes: This is a category entry covering the Shiga Kogen on-mountain accommodation. For English booking, use Snow Monkey Resorts (snowmonkeyresorts.com). Shuttle buses run from Yudanaka Station to Shiga Kogen daily during ski season. Drive from Yudanaka to Hasuike gate: ~30 min on R292 (Orinpikku Kaido). Road closes for heavy snow — check conditions.
short_description: Ski lodges and pensions directly on the Shiga Kogen ski area, primarily Japanese-language booking — Yudanaka is the comfortable English-accessible base town alternative.

amenities: wifi | parking
long_description: Nakano City (中野市) is the closest business-hotel town to Yudanaka, served by the same Nagano Dentetsu line. Options include Toyoko Inn, Dormy Inn, and local business hotels ranging ¥5,000-10,000/night — dramatically cheaper than Yudanaka ryokan. The train from Nakano to Yudanaka takes approximately 15-20 minutes. This option is worth considering for groups on a budget who still want to day-trip to Yudanaka's onsen and restaurants without paying ryokan rates. No onsen on-site at most Nakano business hotels.
name: Nakano City Hotels (Budget Gateway)
notes: Nakano Station to Yudanaka Station: ~15 min on Nagano Dentetsu. Good option for budget travellers wanting to day-trip to onsen and Snow Monkey Park. Tsuruya supermarket (ツルヤ) has a branch near Nakano for self-catering. Nakano IC on the Joshinetsu Expressway provides fast access for drivers.
short_description: Budget business hotels in Nakano City (20 min drive from Yudanaka), useful as a low-cost base with easy train access to Yudanaka Onsen.

amenities: 8 natural spring baths on-site (5 private, 2 indoor communal, 2 outdoor rotenburo) | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Nightly 30-minute cultural building tour | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata and haori jacket provided | Geta sandals for village walks | Air conditioning | Free WiFi | Luggage storage | Station pickup service available
long_description: Founded around 1758 and rebuilt in glorious Showa-era timber, Kanaguya's four-storey illuminated facade on the main cobblestone street is one of the most photographed buildings in Japanese onsen culture. Corridors lit by low lanterns wind like streets between rooms, each uniquely designed. Eight natural spring baths are on-site — five private (no reservation needed, first-come), two indoor communal, and two outdoor rotenburo. A free 30-minute guided cultural tour of the building runs nightly before dinner. Kaiseki dinner and breakfast are included; rooms range from intimate 8-tatami suites to grand multi-room configurations.
name: Rekishi no Yado Kanaguya
short_description: The most iconic inn in Japan — a registered national cultural property whose Showa-era wooden facade is an archetype for Spirited Away.

amenities: 9 indoor baths (16 tubs total) from 6 spring sources | 3 outdoor rotenburo | 2 reservable private baths | 10 rooms with private open-air bath | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Full kaiseki dining (monthly seasonal menu) | Yukata provided | Karaoke | Free parking | Station pickup
long_description: Kokuya stands at the geographical and spiritual heart of Shibu Onsen, operated by the same family for nearly 400 years. The current building dates from 1957 in faithful traditional style. Six distinct spring sources feed nine indoor baths (16 tubs total) — two of which are reservable private baths — plus three outdoor rotenburo, all 100% free-flow natural spring water. Ten rooms include private open-air baths. Kaiseki meals change monthly to reflect seasonality and use Shinshu premium ingredients; guests from overseas particularly appreciate the quality. The kuyu meguri key comes with every room.
name: Shibu Onsen Kokuya
short_description: Established 1625 and now in its 16th generation — nine indoor baths drawing from six spring sources, with private open-air rooms.

amenities: 2 private basement onsens (bookable free of charge) | Communal indoor hot spring bath | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided | Station pickup/luggage delivery on request | Free WiFi
long_description: Run by the Kodama family for generations, Senshinkan Matsuya occupies a multi-storey wooden building right on Shibu's iconic main lane. Eleven tatami rooms — some with birch trees growing through the room, an old-inn quirk beloved by guests. Two private basement onsens can be reserved at no extra charge. Breakfast is notably inventive, changing daily. Stairs are steep; not suitable for those with limited mobility. The Kodamas are known for going above and beyond — luggage delivery, restaurant tips, early check-in if possible.
name: Senshinkan Matsuya
short_description: Beloved 11-room family ryokan on the main cobbled street — warm Kodama-family hospitality, two private onsens bookable free of charge.

amenities: Indoor and outdoor communal hot spring baths | Private outdoor baths in select rooms | Reservable private onsen with sauna | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and Japanese/Western breakfast included | Yukata (colourful selection) provided | Free station pickup | Free WiFi | Bar on-site | Café on-site
long_description: Sakaeya consistently ranks among the highest-reviewed ryokan in Shibu Onsen, praised for exemplary service, exquisite kaiseki (multi-course dinners), and a notable checkout policy allowing guests to stay up to 21 hours from check-in. Rooms are traditional tatami with futon; select rooms include private outdoor baths. The staff greet guests with green tea and seasonal sweets on arrival and go out of their way to assist with local logistics. Both English and Japanese meal requests are accommodated. Colourful yukata selection is a small delight.
name: Shunran no Yado Sakaeya
name_local: 春蘭の宿 さかえや
short_description: Top-rated ryokan in the centre of the village, with private onsen rooms, exceptional kaiseki, and a generous 15-hour stay window.

amenities: See Kokuya listing — identical property
long_description: The property often listed as 'Furuya Ryokan' in English sources is the same inn as Kokuya (古久屋), a frequent transliteration variant. Founded in 1625, this 16th-generation family property remains one of Shibu Onsen's most celebrated inns. Guests receive the same nine-bath internal meguri and the public kuyu key. Please refer to the Kokuya entry for full details. When booking, confirm under the Japanese name 古久屋 or the English site at ichizaemon.com.
name: Furuya Ryokan (Kokuya)
short_description: Note: 'Furuya' (古久屋) is the same establishment as Kokuya — the original romanization of the kanji differs by reading. See Kokuya listing.

amenities: All 28 rooms have private in-room hot spring baths | 1 additional reservable private bath | Heritage public indoor baths (gender-separated) | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner with Shinshu wagyu beef | Breakfast included | Yukata provided | Bar on-site | Restaurant on-site | Massage/spa services | Free parking | Station pickup (meets guests at Yudanaka Station)
long_description: Yorozuya is a substantial ryokan with a history stretching back to the late Edo period, now offering 28 rooms across its main building. Every room comes with its own private hot spring bath — a rare full-property commitment to in-room onsen — plus there is one additional reservable shared private bath. The public indoor baths are heritage-listed spaces. Dinner is the famous Shinshu wagyu beef, handled with a kaiseki precision that draws repeat guests. Both Japanese traditional and Western-style rooms with divan beds are available, making it one of the more accessible options for mixed-preference groups. Rated 9.4 on Expedia. A newer affiliated annex, Shoraiso (opened March 2024), offers five additional suites, all with open-air private baths.
name: Yorozuya
short_description: Grand 28-room heritage inn built around 1789, with all rooms featuring private hot spring baths and a striking heritage public bath.

amenities: 6th-floor panoramic rooftop outdoor rotenburo (all-night access) | Indoor communal baths (male/female) | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata, haori jacket, geta sandals provided | Bluetooth speaker in rooms | Smart toilet | Free WiFi | Free parking | Station pickup (13:00–18:00, reservation required)
long_description: Suminoyu occupies a taller building than most Shibu inns, and makes excellent use of the height: the 6th-floor rooftop open-air bath offers panoramic views over the onsen town roofline to northern Shinshu mountain ranges. All-night bathing available. Rooms blend traditional tatami sensibility with modern comforts — Simmons semi-double beds in the twin rooms, kotatsu tables in tatami rooms, Bluetooth speakers, full smart toilets. Twelve rooms in total; frequently sells out. English spoken. Check-in from 1 PM, which is earlier than most ryokan in the village. Included in Rakuten Travel's recommended listings. Guests receive the kuyu key for the nine public bathhouses.
name: Onyado Suminoyu
short_description: 12-room upscale ryokan with a 6th-floor panoramic rooftop rotenburo and Japanese-modern room interiors that suit solo travellers and couples.

amenities: Indoor and outdoor communal onsen baths | 1 private family bath (bookable) | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast served in-room | Kotatsu heated table in rooms | Yukata provided | Free shuttle from Yudanaka Station (advance booking required) | Free WiFi | Free parking
long_description: Ichinoyu Katei is a compact, characterful ryokan on Shibu Onsen's main street. The springs blend three distinct source types — guests notice the silky, warming quality that the chloride-iron combination creates. Indoor, outdoor, and private family baths are available. Notably, all meals are served in guests' rooms (traditional style), and dinner requires advance reservation (at least 3 days ahead). The free shuttle from Yudanaka Station must be booked in advance. 25 minutes by car to Shiga Kogen. Guests with visible tattoos are advised to use the private bath rather than the communal facilities.
name: Ichinoyu Katei
short_description: Intimate 11-room ryokan with a blend of three spring sources, an in-room kotatsu table, and meals served in guests' own tatami rooms.

amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses (no in-building onsen) | Barista café with specialty coffee (mornings and dinner service) | Yukata and geta provided | Shared modern bathrooms (gender-separated) | Free WiFi | Gift shop | Station shuttle (advance booking required) | Self-set futon bedding
long_description: Koishiya threads an unusual needle: a 100-year-old handcrafted wooden building now operating as a casual inn with dormitory beds, private tatami rooms, and an espresso bar that has developed a cult following. No in-building onsen — instead, guests use their kuyu key to access all nine public bathhouses on foot. No TVs or fridges in rooms; bedding is self-set. The café serves specialty-grade pour-over and espresso (closed for lunch since July 2024; open mornings and dinners). A male-only dormitory option makes it the most budget-accessible bed in the village. Shuttle to Yudanaka Station with advance booking.
name: Shibu Onsen Koishiya Ryokan
short_description: Budget-smart early-Showa-era guesthouse with a renowned barista café; no private onsen, but direct kuyu key access to all nine public baths.

amenities: Communal indoor and outdoor hot spring baths | 1 reservable private outdoor onsen | 1 reservable private indoor onsen | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Free stocked minibar in rooms | Yukata provided | Free WiFi | Free parking | Free station pickup | Gift shop | Tour/ticket assistance
long_description: Shibu Hotel has been welcoming guests since 1935 and has evolved into one of the friendliest and most versatile properties in the village — not too formal, but thoroughly comfortable. Multiple bath options: communal indoor and outdoor baths, one reservable private outdoor bath, and one reservable private indoor bath. Dinner leans heavily on Shinshu ingredients; guests frequently compliment the beef. Staff have been noted for offering vegetarian kaiseki on request. Free stocked minibar in rooms is an unusual and appreciated amenity. Rated 9.8/10 on Expedia. Note: no elevator.
name: Shibu Hotel
short_description: Since 1935, a relaxed mid-range inn with communal, outdoor, and reservable private baths, renowned kaiseki dinner, and free stocked minibars.

amenities: 2 types of reservable private baths (outdoor and indoor) | Communal bath | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner with Shinshu wagyu beef (steak or sukiyaki plan) | Breakfast included | Yukata provided | Free parking
long_description: Ozawaya sits in the middle of Shibu Onsen's main street and is well-regarded for its Shinshu beef kaiseki — menus include Shinshu wagyu steak and Shinshu wagyu sukiyaki options as dedicated plan features. Two distinct private bath types (both exclusively rentable) give guests with tattoos a natural entry point; the tattooed-visitor community has flagged Ozawaya as one of the more accessible properties for private-bath use. Rooms are traditional Japanese style. The official website offers HP-limited pricing that undercuts OTA rates.
name: Ozawaya Ryokan
short_description: Centrally located traditional ryokan offering two types of reservable private baths and signature Shinshu wagyu-centred kaiseki meals.

amenities: Communal onsen baths | Private onsen bookable for exclusive use (surcharge) | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided
long_description: Shimaya is one of those Shibu Onsen properties that gets recommended by travellers who value personal connection over polished luxury. Run by host Ichiro and his wife, the inn is small, traditional, and unhurried. The private onsen (shared in rotation but bookable for exclusive use at a surcharge) is the main draw for guests with tattoos — it's been specifically noted by tattooed visitors as having been welcoming when privacy was arranged in advance. The cobbled main street location places guests right in the heart of village life.
name: Shimaya Ryokan
short_description: A small, personally run inn known for its warm host Ichiro, private onsen access by reservation, and an atmosphere of quiet authenticity.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided | Free parking
long_description: Marukyo is one of the classic mid-scale ryokan that form the backbone of Shibu Onsen's lodging landscape. Fully traditional in layout — tatami rooms, communal baths, yukata walking culture — it offers a more affordable entry into the full kuyu meguri experience. Meals are home-style kaiseki using local ingredients; the inn is small enough that service feels personal. Situated along the main cobblestone street within easy walking of all nine public bathhouses.
name: Marukyo Ryokan
short_description: Traditional small ryokan in the heart of Shibu Onsen with classic tatami rooms and kuyu key access to the nine public bathhouses.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided
long_description: Yumotoya (literally 'inn at the hot spring source') is one of the traditional ryokan listed on the Shibu Onsen official registry. The name references the deep connection to the spring water — Shibu Onsen's waters are among the most mineral-rich in Nagano Prefecture, and properties like Yumotoya have been built around these sources for generations. Standard tatami rooms, communal baths, kuyu meguri key access, and half-board kaiseki follow the village template. Good choice for travellers seeking an affordable, unhurried stay without the premium of flagship properties.
name: Yumotoya Ryokan
short_description: A long-established Shibu ryokan taking its name from the hot spring source itself — 'Yumoto' means the root of the hot water.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided
long_description: Wakaba is among the smaller ryokan in Shibu Onsen, consistently noted for staff warmth and cleanliness. The name means 'young leaves', apt for a property that has a fresh, unpretentious character within an old building. Standard tatami rooms, communal baths, kuyu meguri key, and half-board kaiseki follow the Shibu template. Not to be confused with Wakabaya Shoten, the gelato shop on the main street. Good option for couples or solo travellers wanting an intimate, manageable stay.
name: Wakaba Ryokan
short_description: Warmly rated small ryokan (4.7 on Ctrip) prized for attentive service; quiet and traditional in feel.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses (steps from #9 Shibu-o-yu) | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided
long_description: Hishiya Torazo occupies a quiet corner of Shibu Onsen's upper end, neighbours with Shibu-o-yu (#9 bathhouse, the largest of the nine public baths). This positioning makes it ideal for guests who want to use the public baths frequently without long cobblestone walks in geta. Small, atmospheric, and traditional — the type of inn that defines what Shibu Onsen is. Baths and cooking are frequently praised in reviews. The name, with its tiger motif (torazo), gives the property a playful character.
name: Onyado Hishiya Torazo
short_description: Tucked beside the #9 bathhouse at the top of the village — a serene oasis known for its well-regarded baths and traditional cuisine.

amenities: 1 private outdoor rotenburo garden onsen | 2 additional private indoor baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Breakfast served in-room (dinner available on request) | Yukata provided | Free station pickup and drop-off to monkey park | English spoken by owners | TV in rooms | Fridge in rooms
long_description: Daymaruya is a small, family-operated inn run by a husband and wife couple who have cultivated a devoted following among international visitors. They speak excellent English and handle pickup from Yudanaka Station, drop-off at the Jigokudani Monkey Park trailhead, and general logistics with remarkable care. The private outdoor onsen — set in a quiet garden — is the property's star attraction: guests have described it as 'magical' and worth staying for alone. Three in-house onsens total. Rooms look out over the onsen street and can accommodate families. Breakfast delivered to rooms is excellent. Rated 9.1 on Booking.com. Very popular; books out quickly in ski season.
name: Daymaruya Ryokan
name_local: 貸切露天の宿 大丸屋
short_description: Owner-run budget gem with magical private outdoor onsen, husband-and-wife couple who speak excellent English and drive guests everywhere.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Private outdoor onsen | Kaiseki dinner option | Buffet breakfast | Yukata provided | Free WiFi | Free parking | River views from public baths
long_description: Aburaya Tousen sits on the river between Yudanaka Onsen and Shibu Onsen, slightly outside the main village but sharing the same onsen water culture. The building overlooks the river and the resort town. Facilities include a communal bath, private outdoor bath, and a premium buffet breakfast. Rating of 4.7/5 on Jalan. Buffet breakfast and kaiseki dinner options available. It is one of the gateway-area ryokan popular with visitors to Shiga Kogen — the resort area ski drives are shorter from here than from the deepest part of Shibu village. Phone: 0269-33-3333.
name: Aburaya Tousen
short_description: An elegant riverside ryokan between Yudanaka and Shibu Onsen — river views, refined kaiseki, and a 10-minute drive from Shiga Highlands Roman Museum.

amenities: Indoor and outdoor communal onsen baths | Private reservable onsen | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided | Free station pickup | 2 restaurants on-site | Free WiFi
long_description: Masuya is consistently praised by international travellers as one of Shibu's most complete ryokan experiences: rooms (smaller than average but meticulously designed), kaiseki dinners that have been called 'one of the best', and staff who provide free rides to Yudanaka Station, assist with vegetarian requests, and generally ensure guests don't feel adrift. Both indoor and outdoor onsen baths, with private reservable options. Select rooms have exceptional mountain panoramas. Two on-site restaurants.
name: Wafu-no-Yado Masuya
short_description: Beautifully decorated traditional ryokan with mountain-view rooms, excellent kaiseki, and notable warmth from staff who go the extra distance.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided
long_description: Shiroganeya is one of the registered inns of Shibu Onsen that has drawn positive international visitor reviews for its traditional tatami rooms, genuine onsen atmosphere, and attentive hospitality. The name means 'silver house', a nod to the mercury-mineral clarity of the hot spring water. Like most Shibu properties it operates on a half-board kaiseki model with yukata walking culture built into the stay. Guests receive the kuyu meguri key on check-in.
name: Shiroganeya Ryokan
name_local: 信州渋温泉 渋温泉白銀屋旅館
short_description: Traditional Shibu inn on the official registry, praised for authentic Japanese atmosphere in the heart of the cobblestone district.

address: Near Jigokudani trailhead, Yamanouchi-machi, Shimotakai-gun, Nagano
amenities: Private outdoor rotenburo (41°C, guest use) | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner on advance arrangement | Breakfast included | Yukata provided | Free station pickup | Complementary trailhead transfer | English translated info sheets in rooms
long_description: Minshuku Miyama sits closer to the Jigokudani Monkey Park trailhead than the main Shibu Onsen street, making it a logical base for guests primarily visiting the snow monkeys. Run by a Japanese couple (man in his 60s, wife in the kitchen), the inn has a quietly beautiful outdoor rotenburo heated to 41°C, available to guests at no extra charge. Pre-translated information sheets in English are placed in rooms. The host drives guests from Yudanaka Station and offers a complementary transfer to the Jigokudani trailhead on departure. Kaiseki dinner with advance arrangement. This is simple, honest, Japan-at-home hospitality.
name: Minshuku Miyama
short_description: Quaint minshuku near the Jigokudani trailhead — the owner couple provides translated info sheets, station pickup, and heartfelt service.

amenities: Communal indoor onsen baths | Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses | Kaiseki dinner and breakfast included | Yukata provided
long_description: Takamoto (多喜本) is a registered ryokan in Shibu Onsen that appears in the official accommodation listing by Shibu Onsen Tourism Association. Following the village template, it offers tatami rooms, communal hot spring baths, the kuyu meguri key for the nine public baths, and half-board kaiseki. The name incorporates characters for happiness (多 = many, 喜 = joy), reflecting the traditional naming philosophy of Shibu's inns. A mid-tier option for guests who want the full onsen village experience without the premium of the flagship properties.
name: Onyado Takamoto
short_description: Traditional ryokan in the official Shibu registry — quiet, family-scale, serving the full kuyu meguri and kaiseki experience at moderate pricing.

amenities: natural hot spring (indoor + outdoor) | ski-in/ski-out | base centre on site | rental shop | lift ticket counter | convenience store (Y-Shop) | restaurant (La Mule) | karaoke room | souvenir shop | ski gear storage | coin laundry | free shuttle from Yudanaka Station | free Wi-Fi | yukata
long_description: Hotel Meiko sits literally at the entrance to Mt. KOSHA Yomase Onsen ski resort: the resort's base centre 'Faro' is housed on the hotel's east side, with a rental shop, Yamazaki Y-Shop convenience store, coin lockers and lift-ticket counter. The 41-room hotel offers natural hot spring baths (Meisei-no-yu indoor daiyokujo and an outdoor bath with views over Zenkoji Plain), yukata, and full-board plans with a set-menu Japanese dinner and buffet breakfast. Restaurant La Mule also opens as a slope-side lunch spot in winter. Ski storage, coin laundry and free shuttles from Yudanaka Station are provided. The most operationally convenient base in Yomase.
name: Hotel Meiko (Yomase Rising Sun Hotel)
name_local: よませライジングサンホテル ホテル明幸
short_description: Ski-in/ski-out hotel forming the base centre of Yomase Onsen ski resort — lift tickets, rentals and restaurants all on the ground floor.

long_description: Hotel Selan stands at the foot of Mt. Takayashiro with sweeping views across Zenkoji Plain, the Northern Alps, and the Kita-Shiga Highlands — views good enough to earn the hotel's surroundings a place on Nagano's Sunset-Spot 100 list. The 60-room property (15 Japanese-style, 45 Japanese-Western mix) operates a large 24-hour indoor bath and two open-air baths (including a reservable private rotenburo). Meal plans feature Shinshu rustic cuisine — shabu-shabu with Miyuki pork, Shinshu premium beef, and seasonal local produce. Also functions as a day-trip onsen facility. Shuttle from Yudanaka Station available; basic English spoken at front desk.
name: Hotel Selan
name_local: よませ温泉 ホテルセラン
short_description: Panoramic-view onsen hotel 2 minutes' walk from Yomase ski resort, known for spectacular sunsets over Zenkoji Plain.

long_description: Resort Inn Cairn is a no-frills ski lodge positioned within the Yomase Onsen ski resort boundary, offering direct access to the slopes without a car. The 20 rooms are all Japanese-style tatami, non-smoking; futon self-service. Facilities are ski-practical: ski drying room, coin laundry, large communal bath (Yomase Onsen hot spring), vending machines and Wi-Fi throughout. The lodge caters to ski groups and is accessible by shuttle from Yudanaka Station (pre-booking required). Yukata not provided as standard but available on request from front desk.
name: Resort Inn Cairn (Yomase Onsen)

short_description: Compact 20-room ski lodge inside the Yomase ski area with communal hot-spring bath, ski drying room, and coin laundry.

long_description: Chateautel Kitashiga is a compact Western-style pension-lodge in an old English manor aesthetic, squarely aimed at the Japanese student/young group ski market. The 'ski-yado' format is standard: shared baths (15:00–23:00), set dinner (Shinshu miso nabe all-you-can-eat, 60 minutes), and Japanese-Western set breakfast. Rooms range from twin/family to larger ski-team dorms (2–8 persons). Located 3 minutes' walk to X-JAM Takai Fuji lifts and 3 minutes to the Seven-Eleven. Wi-Fi throughout; free parking (7 cars).
